standard.title: Maximising the Utility of Analytic Products
standard.summary: IC elements shall produce analytic products that customers can easily discover, access, use, and disseminate. Guidance is organised into five principles, listed here in priority order from highest to lowest.

principles.principle: Ensure analysts understand the customer's operating environment --- required information, timeliness, classification limits, and optimal methods for discovery and dissemination. Determine before publication whether the product targets a specific customer or a general audience.

Analytic products must give customers insight into source quality and credibility, characterise the uncertainty of judgments, and include context to aid understanding. All products shall adhere to the standards of analytic tradecraft in ICD 203.

Create products for timely dissemination to US customers (federal, state, local, tribal) and, where permitted, partners (Five Eyes, NATO). When similar credible information is reported at multiple classification levels, use the lowest level to facilitate re-use.
Produce tearlines at the lowest classification level that protects sensitive data, sources, methods, and activities (per ICD 209).
All analytic products must employ proper sourcing in line with ICD 206, enabling readers to locate and retrieve sources per ICD 501 while avoiding exhaustive listings.
Use alternate versions, portion marking, sanitised text, metadata tagging, and tearlines to facilitate tailored re-use. Sanitised products must remain congruent with their higher-classified versions in facts, judgments, confidence levels, and probabilistic language.

principle.name: Make Analytic Products Discoverable and Accessible

principles.principle: Ensure that customers with proper clearances and approved mission need can discover and access analytic products per ICD 501. At minimum, disseminate products electronically to the Library of National Intelligence or its successor systems.
Adhere to the Principles of Intelligence Transparency --- enhancing public understanding of intelligence activities while protecting sensitive sources and methods.
